craft_claim: Objectivity movements recur independently — French chosisme (Robbe-Grillet), German Neue Sachlichkeit, Japanese shasei, Chinese baimiao — each defining a neutral descriptive register, not a universal code.

supporting_evidence.location: Essays collected in Pour un nouveau roman (e.g., 'Nature, humanism, tragedy')
supporting_evidence.note: Robbe-Grillet argues for a neutral registering of sensations and things and against the humanist-tragic frame, a French instance of an objective descriptive program.

supporting_evidence.location: Chapters on the movement's meaning and literature
supporting_evidence.note: Neue Sachlichkeit (term coined by Hartlaub, 1925) produced a literature of non-sentimental, emotionless reporting with precise detail and veneration for 'the fact,' while remaining politically motivated.
Masaoka Shiki's shasei ('sketch from life') rejects ornamental fantasy for realistic observation of nature, an independent Japanese instance of plain observed-fact description.

supporting_evidence.location: Reference-work entry on baimiao (plain line drawing)
supporting_evidence.note: Baimiao denotes an unembellished, subtractive plain-line descriptive register in Chinese art and narrative, a further independent analogue.

counterevidence.note: Section C 'Contested status' and section E item 6 record that Neue Sachlichkeit's neutrality was politically loaded and that 'objectivity' is a stance with an agenda, not a view from nowhere, so the shared neutral descriptive register these movements define is contested at its centre.

scope: Cross-cultural survey of objectivity traditions; scoped per tradition, not asserted as a universal aesthetic.
exceptions: These movements differ in motive (soteriological, perceptual, political, anti-humanist) and are not the same stance; only the surface technique of withholding affect recurs.
